To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ingestion of a fish protein hydrolyzate concurrently with carbohydrate and whey protein does not improve performance in a 5 min TT following a 90 minute submaximal cycling task.
the addition of a fish protein hydrolyzate did not influence 5 km performance time, but it did influence metabolism during the exercise.
the ingestion of CHO, PRO, and CHO-PRO with PEP did not improve performance in the 5 KM TT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of marine peptide hydrolysates as an adjunct to carbohydrate and whey protein ingestion during endurance exercise.
the effect of carbohydrate (CHO) ingestion on exercise performance.
the effect of carbohydrate (CHO) ingestion on endurance exercise performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of hydrolysates to a carbohydrate solution did not improve endurance performance.
the addition of hydrolysate marine peptides did not improve endurance performance in this study.
the addition of hydrolysate marine peptides to a CHO and whey protein supplement did not provide an additive effect in terms of exercise performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inclusion of a fish protein hydrolyzate with carbohydrate and whey protein does not improve performance during a 5-km time trial.
hydrolyzed marine peptide supplementation may have a role as a potential ergogenic aid, but further investigation is needed.
the ingestion of CHO-PRO- PEP during exercise did not enhance endurance exercise performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of marine peptides to a CHO and whey protein beverage does not provide any ergogenic benefit during prolonged endurance exercise.
the addition of marine peptides to carbohydrate and whey protein ingestion does not provide any ergogenic benefits during exercise.
a fish protein hydrolyzate may have a negative influence on endurance exercise metabolism, and this needs further research.
